context:
Sandbox subsystem tests (intellicrack.sandbox.* analysis modules, manager/orchestration, and the SandboxBridge). Context:

- Analysis modules (extract_iocs, generate_timeline, match_behaviors, detect_c2_patterns, diff_reports) are PURE functions over an ExecutionReport / activity dicts - drive them with a REAL constructed ExecutionReport (or real captured activity records) and assert the exact decoded result against an independent oracle (recompute the expected IOC set / timeline ordering / behavior match a different way; e.g. parse the same network_activity yourself and assert the extracted IPs/domains exactly). Never assert isinstance/not-None/len>=0; assert the concrete extracted values.

- Manager/lifecycle tests: drive the real SandboxManager instance registry / state machine and assert the concrete state transition (instance id present, state.status value, eviction/cache behavior counted via a real import_module counter). The external sandbox backend (QEMU process, Windows container, a live VM/socket) is the ONLY permitted double - stub it at that subprocess/socket boundary; never mock the manager or analysis function under test.

- A QEMU/Windows-backend test that needs the real emulator/container legitimately SKIPS when it is absent - keep those environment-capability skips. Everything else must run headless and assert real decoded state.

- base_types: dataclass/enum/serialization tests must assert real round-trip equality (dataclass_to_dict -> reconstruct, or json_safe output structure) against an independently constructed expected dict, not that a field merely exists.
